title: Redwood demo - Data handling & retention controls (Lakemere Financial)
action_items: Maya Chen: Share SOC2 and ISO docs + security datasheet - Due: 2026-03-06
Ethan Ruiz: Try the private deployment quickstart in our sandbox and report infra questions - Due: 2026-03-13
Liam Ortiz: Run a short benchmark for their 1k req/day profile and share perf/cost estimate - Due: 2026-03-09
next_steps: Send security pack and SOC2 attestations
Schedule a 1-hr POC kickoff (dedicated capacity) next week
Share step-by-step for turning off request storage + audit log examples
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood here, i have Liam with me, Liam's our solutions engineer. we're going to walk through data handling controls: redaction, retention toggles, request storage, and what Private/VPC options look like.
[00:12] Priya Kapoor: Hi Maya, thanks. I'm Priya, Head of Security at Lakemere. Ethan and Carla are with me as well. high level — we need to know how to keep PII out of logs and meet our retention policy (7 years for certain audit trails) and show auditors.
[00:30] Liam Ortiz: Great — quick agenda: API-level toggles (request storage off/on), console UI for retention, automated redaction rules, and private deployment options incl. KMS/HSM keys. We'll demo the console screens and a sample API call.
[01:05] Ethan Ruiz: Quick Q up front — can we completely disable request storage for some routes and keep it for others? we have mixed workloads.
[01:18] Liam Ortiz: Yes you can. We have per-route request storage toggles — you can set default to off and opt-in specific routes. it's also available via our SDK headers for programmatic control. note: if you turn storage off, certain observability features (eg token-level cost breakdown) are limited.
[01:42] Carla Mendes: when storage's off, do you still emit audit logs? we need an audit trail for admin actions even if user request payloads are not stored.
[01:53] Maya Chen: short answer: yes — admin/audit logs (config changes, auth events) are separate and retained per your retention settings. request body storage is opt-in/opt-out.
[02:08] Priya Kapoor: ok show us the redaction. we have card numbers and ssn leaking in prompts.
[02:15] Liam Ortiz: sure — we'll use the console. pulling up the Data Handling tab... link to demo deck: https://redwood-internal.com/decks/data-handling-demo (shared)
[02:30] [screen share noise] Liam Ortiz: here you see a list of projects, each project has a Data policy. you can add redaction rules: regex, key path rules for JSON, and ML-based entity scrubbing. regex example for PAN numbers, and a rule to strip out explicit keys like "ssn". the ML scrubbing runs as a preprocessor and is tunable — not perfect but catches common PII.
[03:05] Ethan Ruiz: is ML scrubbing on by default? can we run it in audit-only mode first?
[03:12] Liam Ortiz: yes — audit-only mode exists, it tags matches in logs but doesn't remove until you flip to enforcement. good for tuning.
[03:28] Priya Kapoor: what's the risk of false positives removing content we need for model quality? we have prompts with alphanumeric tokens that look like PANs sometimes.
[03:38] Liam Ortiz: you'll see an allowlist and an override path — you can whitelist specific keys or patterns. plus our Optimize recommendations suggest conservative regexes if your workload shows collisions.
[03:55] Carla Mendes: can redaction happen in the private deployment too? we can't send raw request bodies to Redwood's hosted logs.
[04:03] Maya Chen: yes. in Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, redaction runs in-customer environment. logs can be configured to ship to your S3 or internal ELK, and the control plane can be set to not retain payloads.
[04:20] Priya Kapoor: KMS — we need envelope encryption with our key that never leaves AWS KMS.
[04:28] Liam Ortiz: supported. you can plug in your KMS/HSM — we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own HSM via standard APIs. keys can be used for at-rest encryption of stored requests and for signing audit logs.
[04:45] Ethan Ruiz: any compliance attestation that private mode meets our auditors' bar?
[04:52] Maya Chen: we have customers using Private to meet strict data residency and audit needs; we'll share SOC2, ISO27001 snapshots, and a whitepaper on Private deployments. that's in the next steps.
[05:10] [06:00] Speaker 1: so about retention periods — you mentioned per-tenant retention. can we do different retention for embeddings vs request payloads vs logs?
[06:15] Liam Ortiz: yes, retention is broken into buckets: request payloads, embeddings, model cache/KV, and audit logs. each can be configured by policy. embeddings are a common concern — we provide auto-scrub options before indexing (hashing, truncation).
[06:35] Priya Kapoor: hashing embeddings still a risk; what about deterministic re-identification if someone has the original text?
[06:42] Liam Ortiz: good point. we recommend one-way salt+hash and optionally irreversible dimensionality transforms. Optimize can suggest balance between accuracy and irreversibility.
[06:58] Ethan Ruiz: how do you handle conference calls where transcripts might contain PII? do you store them?
[07:05] Maya Chen: call transcriptions are considered request-derived artifacts and follow the same storage controls. you can disable transcript storage and have on-the-fly streaming only.
[07:22] Priya Kapoor: auditors ask for proof of deletion. can you provide tamper-evident deletion logs?
[07:30] Liam Ortiz: we can produce deletion events in the audit log and sign them. for private deployments you can configure cross-checks with your KMS to ensure keys were rotated/deleted.
[07:45] Carla Mendes: what about telemetry? i mean the runtime emits metrics — do those include token-level info that could be sensitive?
[07:52] Liam Ortiz: telemetry is aggregative by default; token-level traces are optional and stored only if request storage is enabled. also there's a scrub stage before telemetry export.
[08:10] [09:00] Priya Kapoor: let's focus on the API example for toggling request storage.
[09:12] Liam Ortiz: ok example: POST /v1/requests with header X-Redwood-Store: false will submit without storing. show code snippet in the console --> (reads) "curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer x' -H 'X-Redwood-Store: false' -d '{\"prompt\":\"...\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate". note caveat: some downstream features require storage.
[09:50] Ethan Ruiz: can we have a policy engine that enforces store=false for any route tagged "prod-payment"?
[09:58] Liam Ortiz: yes — route tagging + policy rules. you can create policy: if route contains prod-payment then force storage=false and add redaction profile payments.
[10:12] Priya Kapoor: great. about logs retention — we need 7 years for admin logs; can Redwood hold that without storage costs blowing up?
[10:22] Maya Chen: audit logs are compressed, archival tiering available. we provide an export connector to S3 Glacier or your archival system. pricing reflects archival storage.
[10:35] [12:00] Carla Mendes: is there UI to show what was redacted? our QA team needs to verify redaction didn't remove contextual tokens.
[12:10] Liam Ortiz: yes, audit-only mode shows annotated events with highlighted matches and allowlist overrides. it's in the console under Data -> Redaction history.
[12:28] Priya Kapoor: about RBAC, we need separation: developers can see logs but not raw PII; security team sees raw for incident response.
[12:36] Liam Ortiz: RBAC is role-based with fine-grained permissions. you can mask fields at role-level; for example, dev role sees masked tokens, sec role sees full (if allowed by policy). all accesses are logged.
[12:55] Ethan Ruiz: SSO? we use Okta with SCIM groups.
[13:02] Maya Chen: SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning supported. you can map SCIM groups to RBAC roles in the console.
[13:18] [15:00] Priya Kapoor: performance impact — running ML-based PII scrub adds latency?
[15:10] Liam Ortiz: small impact, usually 20–40 ms pre-processing. for high qps we recommend edge pre-scrub or sample-based scrub then enforcement in async path. Optimize will advise batching/caching to mitigate.
[15:35] Maya Chen: here's a quick cost/latency slide — (reads) hosted mode with storage off defaults cheaper but loses some diagnostics; dedicated pools cost more but give predictable latency.
[15:55] Ethan Ruiz: any customers in finance doing retention 7 years on audit logs?
[16:03] Maya Chen: yes, multiple customers in banking use our dedicated + private combo and archive logs to S3 Glacier. we'll share references.
[16:20] Priya Kapoor: about legal hold — sometimes we need to prevent deletion for an investigation. can you apply holds?
[16:28] Liam Ortiz: yes, legal hold prevents policy-based deletion until release; those are recorded in audit logs as a state change.
[16:40] Carla Mendes: let's talk about embeddings again. we use embeddings for search — can we purge embeddings for certain users on request?
[16:48] Liam Ortiz: yes, per-user embedding deletion is supported; you can tag embeddings with user-id and run targeted deletes which also emit deletion events.
[17:05] Priya Kapoor: show me the API for deletion.
[17:12] Liam Ortiz: DELETE /v1/embeddings?tag=user:12345 — returns job id for async deletion. you can track status with /jobs/{id}.
[17:28] Ethan Ruiz: nice. about monitoring: if storage is disabled, our SREs still need error traces to troubleshoot. any best practices?
[17:36] Liam Ortiz: we suggest a dual-path: store minimal error context (no payload), use hashed correlation ids to replay traces for authorized sec users. also sample 0.1% full payloads in audit-only mode for debugging with strict allowlist.
[17:58] Priya Kapoor: ok, let's cover private deployment specifics.
[18:05] Maya Chen: Private includes a customer-managed control plane and data plane in your VPC. you control network egress, storage endpoints, and KMS. Redwood provides the orchestration and the runtime images.
[18:22] Ethan Ruiz: what's the timeline to spin up Private?
[18:27] Liam Ortiz: typical POC in 2–4 weeks for a small footprint, full production depends on sizing. initial provisioning usually a week if infra approvals are fast.
[18:45] Priya Kapoor: and support SLAs?
[18:48] Maya Chen: dedicated customers can get SLA-backed latency and uptime and a named CSM. details in the enterprise pack.
[19:05] Carla Mendes: any hard limits on redaction rules or regex performance?
[19:12] Liam Ortiz: regex runs in a sandboxed engine; very complex regex can be slower and we recommend precompiled rules. for high throughput we recommend key-path rules which are O(1).
[19:30] [21:00] Priya Kapoor: compliance question again — do you keep data lineage so auditors can show chain of custody?
[21:10] Liam Ortiz: lineage recorded in audit logs: creation, redaction, deletion events, key rotations, and export operations — all timestamped and signed.
[21:35] Maya Chen: quick recap before we close?
[21:42] Priya Kapoor: yes please.
[21:45] Maya Chen: recap: per-route request storage toggles, audit-only redaction mode, KMS/HSM support for private deployments, per-bucket retention and archive to S3 glacier, embeddings tagging + targeted deletion, RBAC + SCIM mapping, legal hold support, and deletion/audit events are available. next steps — we will share the SOC2 pack and a Private POC design doc, Liam will run the perf/cost benchmark, and Ethan will trial the private quickstart.
[22:20] Ethan Ruiz: thanks — that's helpful.
[22:25] Carla Mendes: please include sample policies for our infra team.
[22:30] Maya Chen: will do — we'll send policy templates.
[22:40] Priya Kapoor: thanks all.
[22:45] [call ends]
summary: Redwood demo for Lakemere Financial focused on data handling and retention. Covered per-route request storage toggles, redaction (regex + ML scrubbing with audit-only mode), private deployment options with KMS/HSM integration, retention buckets (requests, embeddings, audit logs), embedding deletion, RBAC/SCIM mapping, legal hold, and audit/deletion events. Next steps include sharing SOC2 and Private POC docs, a perf/cost benchmark, and trying the private quickstart.
